items.question: Why did the Apollo 13 oxygen tank explode?

result.answer: The thermostatic switches were rated for 28 volts DC but did not operate correctly at the 65 volts DC used during testing. [ntrs:20110015690] Launch personnel did not know the thermostatic switches were not rated to open with 65 volts DC ground power applied. [nasa:apollo13-review-board]

items.question: What happened during the Mir fire?

result.answer: On February 24, 1997, a fire ignited in an oxygen generating system aboard the Russian space station Mir. [nasa:mir-fire-25-years] The fire cut off access to one of the two Soyuz escape vehicles and filled the station's modules with smoke. [nasa:mir-fire-25-years] The six crew members extinguished the flames, and the station's structure was not damaged. [nasa:mir-fire-25-years]

claims.text: The six crew members extinguished the flames, and the station's structure was not damaged.

items.question: How is smoke different in microgravity?

result.answer: In low gravity, buoyant flow is negligible, so smoke particles concentrate near the source and take longer to reach detectors. [ntrs:20170007283] Microgravity fires have significantly different structure than fires in normal gravity, which can change how smoke particles form. [ntrs:20170007283]

claims.text: In low gravity, buoyant flow is negligible, so smoke particles concentrate near the source and take longer to reach detectors.
claims.excerpt: In low gravity, buoyant flow is negligible which causes particles to concentrate at the smoke source, increasing their residence time, and increasing the transport time to smoke detectors.

claims.text: Microgravity fires have significantly different structure than fires in normal gravity, which can change how smoke particles form.
claims.excerpt: Microgravity fires have significantly different structure than those in 1-g which can change the formation history of the smoke particles.
